newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares slide at close, volumes hit pre-FOMC.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares slide at close, volumes hit pre-FOMC.

text.p: Dutch shares slid down in late trading as early losses on Wall Street reinforced slight weakness seen throughout the day in Europe, dealers said.
The AEX index of leading shares closed down 6.85 points at 787.45 as Dow Industrial index lost over 50 points and the dollar remained weak, barely above 1.90 guilders.
In the morning, chartists were already less bullish than a week ago as the AEX backed firmly away from the 800 mark reached on Friday.
"The AEX index is quickly losing momentum at the upper side of its rising trend channel," said ING Barings' weekly outlook.
Trading on Tuesday was muted as the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting starting later today -- and a possible rise of U.S. interest rates -- distracted most players.
"There's a real sit-and-wait feel for the moment," one trader said.
In the weaker market, financials performed better than most and attracted reasonable volumes. ING shares ended up 40 cents at 80.10 while ABN AMRO closed 10 cents higher at 35.00 guilders.

Dealers said the market was viewing positively the forthcoming listing of both banks in the United States and the prospects. ABN AMRO shares are listed from Wednesday. ING enters the market on June 13.
"It seems they'll both get a positive reception in the U.S," one trader said.
Unilever, however, tumbled, ending down 7.50 guilders at 377.90. Many players were unsure why the stock had fallen so far, saying there was no clear triggering of selling points.

Others said the market was becoming nervous since the company's announcement it would sell its chemicals speciality units to ICI had boosted the share price. They said the lack of any clear planned use of the proceeds had hit the stock.
"They have to do something with the money. It's not going to gain just sitting in the bank," one trader said.
